items.definition:
the beliefs or opinions that are generally held about someone or something
The restaurant has a good reputation for its food.

an evaluation or judgment
The teacher gave a fair assessment of the student's progress.

a striking difference between two things
There was a sharp contrast between their opinions.

the act of making something longer or larger
They requested an extension for the project deadline.

a person who establishes an institution or settlement
She is the founder of a successful tech company.

the state of being extremely poor
Many organizations are working to reduce poverty worldwide.

the process or a period of changing from one state or condition to another
The transition from school to university can be challenging.

a chemical substance that tastes sour, reacts with metals, and turns litmus paper red
Lemon juice is an acid.

a feeling of worry, nervousness, or unease
She felt a lot of anxiety before her exam.

a male ruler of a small independent state or a nobleman of the highest rank
The duke attended the royal wedding.

the act of compelling observance of or compliance with a law, rule, or obligation
Law enforcement is responsible for maintaining order.

a mathematical relationship or rule expressed in symbols
The scientist developed a new formula for the chemical reaction.

a punishment imposed for breaking a law, rule, or contract
The referee awarded a penalty kick.

a statement or action expressing disapproval of or objection to something
The students organized a protest against the tuition fees.

publication
The new scientific publication was widely discussed.

assault
The police are investigating the assault.

awareness
There is growing public awareness of environmental issues.

component
Each component of the machine must work perfectly.

expectation
His performance exceeded all expectations.

exposure
Prolonged exposure to the sun can be harmful.

guarantee
The product comes with a five-year guarantee.

legend
The local legend tells of a hidden treasure.

a position in a hierarchy
He holds a high rank in the army.

a promise or firm decision to do something
She showed great commitment to her studies.

an intense feeling of fear, shock, or disgust
The news filled them with horror.

result; production
The factory's output increased this quarter.

health, happiness, and fortunes of a person or group
The government is responsible for the welfare of its citizens.

the art or practice of designing and constructing buildings
The city is famous for its modern architecture.

in the interest of; as a representative of
He spoke on behalf of the entire team.

the study of how societies use scarce resources
She is studying economics at university.

a business or organization; the ruling class of a society
It's a well-known establishment in the city center.

a fundamental truth or belief
He lives by strong moral principles.

an act of helping or encouraging
The good news gave him a confidence boost.

government department; chest of drawers
He works for a government bureau.

a military rank
The colonel commanded the regiment.

the gradual development of something
The evolution of technology is rapid.

a sudden brilliant or creative idea
His music is a great source of inspiration for me.

a monument or statue established to remind people of a person or event
They built a memorial to honor the fallen soldiers.

a smaller number or part
The decision was made by a small minority of the members.

a person acknowledged as holy or virtuous
Saint Patrick is the patron saint of Ireland.

a union or association formed for mutual benefit
The two countries formed an alliance.

an offer of a price, especially at an auction
She made a high bid for the painting.

a head of a college or university faculty or department
The dean announced the new policy.

the state of owning something
The company changed ownership last year.

purpose; benefit
For goodness sake, hurry up!

a person who expresses an unfavorable opinion of something
The film critic gave the movie a bad review.

a foolish or stupid person
Don't be an idiot, think before you act.

a legal agreement by which a bank lends money at interest in exchange for taking title to the debtor's property
They took out a mortgage to buy their house.

the action or fact of making something smaller or less in amount, degree, or size
There was a significant reduction in costs.

a person who carries out academic or scientific research
The researcher published a new study.

change, alteration
They proposed an amendment to the constitution.

high-ranking clergyman
The bishop delivered a sermon.

productivity, effectiveness
The new system improved the efficiency of the process.

business, undertaking
Starting a new enterprise requires courage.

discovery, conclusion
The research findings were published last week.

public meeting place, discussion group
The online forum was a place for lively debate.

head of the Catholic Church
The Pope delivered his blessing.

farming
Modern agriculture relies heavily on technology.

trade; business
International commerce is vital for global economies.

deception; trickery
He was arrested for credit card fraud.

respect; privilege
It was an honour to meet her.

person who comes to live permanently in a foreign country
Many immigrants contribute to the economy.

something handed down from the past
The artist left a lasting legacy.

proportion; relationship between two numbers
The ratio of boys to girls in the class is 2:1.
